title: Choose the transistor's base resistor
story: The microcontroller's PWM pin (3.3 V when high) switches the night light's NPN transistor through a base resistor in slot S1. The transistor connects the white LED and its 68 ohm resistor to ground, from the 4.5 V battery. With the pin high, the LED must get between 15 and 20 mA (the transistor fully on), and the pin must not have to supply more than 5 mA. The transistor's current gain is about 100.

goals.label: the pin supplies at most 5 mA

hints: Base current = (3.3 V - 0.7 V) / R. The transistor can pass at most about 100 times that.
The LED needs about 19 mA, so the base needs comfortably more than 0.19 mA, but not tens of mA.
